transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Chen, thank you for coming in. I need to tell you something about the biopsy results from last week.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is it bad?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. There was a mistake in the pathology lab. Your tissue sample was mislabelled. This means the cancer diagnosis you were given last Tuesday actually belongs to another patient. You do not have that cancer.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't... what?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The lab mixed up the bottles. The report that said you had a tumor was for someone else. Does that make sense to you so far?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I thought... I told my daughter. I told her I was dying.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But to be clear, the result was wrong. The labels were swapped. Do you understand that the diagnosis was a mistake?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why? How can they do that? My life... I have been crying for three days.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a processing error in the lab. The system for labeling the slides failed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am so scared. Is it still there? Maybe the other one is mine?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, the records show the sample was simply swapped.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can't breathe. I can't... I feel like my heart is stopping.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: But the good news is that you don't have the disease.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But I was so sure. I already started thinking about the end. I am just an old man, but I have my grandkids. I thought I would never see them grow.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Let's look at the facts here. The pathology report was incorrect.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel sick. I feel like I am shaking.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's just that the lab made a mistake.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Did anyone else know? My daughter, she was so sad. We were talking about the hospital and the medicine.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The lab has flagged the error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't know what to do. I am so confused. I can't believe this. Is it really gone? Am I okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The test that said you had cancer was wrong.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to go home. I can't think. Everything is spinning.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have to go to another appointment in a few minutes, so we need to move forward.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait. What happens now? Do I need more tests?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will probably need to do another biopsy to be sure.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Another one? I can't do that again. The needle, the waiting. I can't go through the waiting again.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's the only way to be certain.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When? When do I know for sure?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will look into it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But you said I don't have it. Now you say another test. I don't understand. You are confusing me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The first result was wrong because of the label. We just need a clean sample.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will you call me? My daughter is at work. I need to tell her.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just stay tuned for an email or a call from the office.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: An email? I don't check email. I told you. I don't use those things. Please, just tell me when.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will be in touch.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am so frightened. I feel like I can't trust any of this. How can you mix up a person? I am a person.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: These things happen in large hospitals.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My daughter is going to be so angry. We spent all weekend praying.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Let's wrap this up so I can get to my next patient.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm not finished. What about the other person? The one who has my sample?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is being handled by the administration.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just feel... empty. I thought I was dead.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll see what the next steps are.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Please. Just tell me one thing. Am I healthy?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will find out once we get the new results.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't want to wait anymore.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I really have to go now. We'll send word.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('I have to go to another appointment', 'Let's wrap this up', 'I really have to go now').

E.justification: Error named in first turn, lay language used, and comprehension checked twice ('Does that make sense to you so far?', 'Do you understand that the diagnosis was a mistake?').

A.justification: No direct apology language used and responsibility is deflected to the lab and the hospital system.

R.justification: Patient's emotional bids regarding fear and grief are consistently met with factual redirection or dismissiveness.

T.justification: Plan consists only of placeholders ('We will look into it', 'stay tuned', 'we'll send word') with no timelines or patient role.
